svg.text: RED
WHITE
what it should come to
BUILD ONE
1. Cut all three out. Cut the slit in the black with a knife — it is a cut, not a fold.
2. Score the black on both dashed lines, fold both halves FORWARD onto the middle disc, then
open them again. That tells you which face of each half ends up on the outside.
3. Glue the red to the outward face of the upper half and the white to the outward face of the
lower half. Line the red’s bite up with the black’s round lobe — then the 4 mm of colour
hanging past the black lands evenly. Leave the white’s tongue unglued.
4. Fold the white half forward first, then the red half forward over it.
5. Feed the tongue up BEHIND the red half, through the slit, and fold it back down on its dashed
line. The disc lands in the middle and holds both halves shut.
WHAT TO WATCH FOR
Slit 14.6 mm, button 17.8 mm — 1.6 mm of catch a side. If the disc will not go
through, lengthen the slit 1 mm at a time; if it falls back out, shorten it.
No black should show at the rim: the colour overhangs it by 4 mm. If any does, the colour is
more than 4 mm out of place — tell me and I will widen the overhang.
Neck 15.1 mm at each hinge — tell me if it feels like it will tear in heavier stock.
Foil can crack along a fold: score it properly first, and fold away from the foil side.
50 mm — print at 100%, actual size, no “fit to page”
